What degraded

  • The deck did not ship. It is held under the 7.01 ratchet floor after five scoring rounds, and the pull request is open and ready but not merged. Shipping it needs an owner_override in runs/carousel/2026-09-24/score.json.
  • A robots violation during re-verification. Three agenda pages were fetched on public.destinyhosted.com, whose robots file disallows this fetcher, because a single-line robots.txt was read as empty. The bodies were deleted and back nothing. A fourth fetch first logged as a violation, on taylortx.new.swagit.com, was not one. The fix is the daily lane's, since reverify.py has no robots reader, and the proposal is in the upgrade backlog.
  • The artwork never cleared the craft judges' showstopper cap. The count frame, the capsule people, the box houses and the sprite grass are the reasons every craft card gave.
  • The Supabase ask-pack step was not run, and the web edition's article page was not built, because the deck is held.

Named here rather than left out. A run that quietly ships less than it planned teaches nobody anything.

Post this

Upload the PDF to LinkedIn as a document, title it FAA draft on Zipline drone delivery in Texas, comments close October 11th, paste the post copy under it, then paste the first comment within a minute of posting.

carousel.pdf   contact sheet   the site

1. The post copy

A pod comes down 330 feet on a line.

Zipline wants FAA approval to begin drone package delivery in Amarillo, Austin, El Paso, Houston and San Antonio. The FAA's draft environmental assessment of the plan is open for comment. The draft says Zipline prepared it under FAA supervision.

At a delivery the aircraft would hover about 75 seconds. On the way down the pod steers itself sideways and evaluates the spot. The draft says an image goes to an operator when the pod can't identify the target and judge it. It gives no figure for how often.

The last slide carries the FAA's comment address. Comments close October 11th. Will the final version say how often an operator is sent an image?

#FAA #Zipline #Texas

Every change is logged in ledger/carousel/upgrades.json.

Notes

The record came first. 38 items were re-verified and the due list fell from 52 to 13, every one of them at a measured access boundary. Two items were admitted. tx-2026-0186 is the FAA draft environmental assessment of Zipline drone delivery in five Texas metros, open for comment until October 11th. tx-2026-0187 is the PUCT's 16 TAC 25.194 order. The scoring panel's integrity findings were carried into the record and the web edition: the noise finding now reads as the draft states it, the Remote Pilot in Command is named, and the FAA page title is corrected.

This is a draft. Nothing was sent. The deck did NOT merge, so nothing here is on main and there is nothing to post. The links resolve against the run branch for as long as it exists.
